messages:
Ava (product): Filing a PRD intake for 'Degraded Mode' semantics. Problem: when we fall back (quantized model, smaller variant, cached response, or soft-queueing) customers see unpredictable behavior and different quality/latency tradeoffs. Need a clear contract: problem statement, goals, non-goals, acceptance criteria, and success metrics. Feedback please — trying to get to a minimal spec we can ship as a canary.

Sam (eng): Quick clarification — by degraded modes do we mean: (A) model variant fallback, (B) cached/served-from-prefix, (C) queued/soft-throttle returning a shorter response, or (D) region/failover fallback? We should enumerate and attach perf targets per mode.

Priya (eng-ml): +1. For (A) model fallback we need quality gating. Proposal: require customer-configurable eval thresholds; default: no more than X% relative drop on their eval suite. We'll need a harness to run tenant prompt sets against both variants. Can't choose a single universal X without tenant evals.

Maya (design): From UX pov we must keep response schema stable. Suggest adding two optional fields: `served_variant` and `degradation_reason` so integrators can opt-in to handle fallbacks. Non-goal: changing token-level streaming format. Keep token stream identical unless explicitly switching variant mid-stream.

Diego (eng-sre): Ops constraints: different offerings get different guarantees. For Dedicated we can offer a 'best-effort degraded mode' with no SLA. For Hosted API we need to decide whether fallback is SLA-covered. Suggested guardrail: if fallback used, p95 latency must remain <= 2x normal p95 and absolute <= 750ms for typical <512 token requests. Also: telemetry must include per-request tag and sampling of full outputs for auditing.

Liam (solutions): Customers are asking for an explicit header like `X-Redwood-Degraded: true` and a confidence delta so product can surface to end-users. We already have tenant routing feature flags — we can reuse those for canary routing.

Juno (qa): Acceptance checklist idea: 1) response schema includes fields documented, 2) unit/integration tests simulate each fallback mode, 3) end-to-end eval on 3 representative prompt families (happy path, long context, instruction-heavy), 4) performance under 75th/95th percentile load. Also request automated regression alert that triggers on quality delta breach.

Ava (product): Draft acceptance criteria (proposal):
- Behavior: when a fallback/degraded path is used, the response envelope MUST include `served_variant` and `degraded_reason` (both optional but recommended for backwards compat).
- Quality: default guardrail = no more than 7% relative drop on a standardized nDCG/accuracy metric OR no more than 10 percentage points drop on customer-designed eval score (tenant-configurable).
- Latency: p95 fallback latency <= 2x p95 normal and absolute p95 <= 750ms for requests <512 tokens.
- Observability: per-request tag `degraded=true`, metric `degraded_rate` by tenant, `fallback_latency_p95`, and a daily digest summarizing degraded requests and sample outputs.
- Rollout: canary to 5% of tenants, with auto-rollback if customer eval delta > configured threshold or degraded_rate > alert threshold for 1h.

Sam (eng): Implementation notes: will need router policy updates, model-catalog flags to mark compatible fallbacks, and a tiny change to the response envelope. Risk: some clients parse token stream/string; even small schema additions may break naive parsers. Suggest making `served_variant` non-breaking and documented in SDK release notes.

Priya (eng-ml): Edge cases: 1) nondeterministic fallback behavior (same prompt sometimes the base model, sometimes fallback) — prefer sticky routing per session id to reduce flakiness. 2) prompt-sensitive quality where fallback only fails on narrow prompts — need per-prompt telemetry. 3) when fallback occurs mid-stream (streaming switch) — try to avoid; prefer finishing with one variant per request.

Maya (design): Confirming non-goals: we will NOT do model result merging or re-ranking between variants as part of this. We also are NOT defining new end-user UI for degraded notices beyond the header/fields.

Diego (eng-sre): Monitoring/alerts to add: 
- `degraded_rate` per-tenant (alert if >10% sustained for 24h)
- `fallback_latency_p95` (alert if > 2x baseline)
- `quality_delta_avg` (if we can calculate)
- `auto_rollback_events` count.
Include SLO notes: fallbacks are excluded from standard SLA unless explicitly covered in tenant contract.

Ava (product): Action items & timeline:
- Eng/ML (Sam/Priya): propose config knobs + reasonable default thresholds by Tue.
- SRE (Diego): define alert thresholds, retention, and required telemetry fields by Tue.
- QA (Juno): draft test cases and canary test plan by Wed.
- Design (Maya): produce minimal JSON schema example and SDK notes by Wed.
- Solutions (Liam): collect prompt examples from top-5 tenants and confirm willingness to participate in canary.
I'll consolidate into a short PRD mid-week and link.

Sam (eng): Example minimal response we can include in PRD: 
```json
{
  "id": "req_abc123",
  "served_variant": "redwood-3b-quantized-v2",
  "degraded_reason": "capacity_fallback",
  "output": {"text": "..."} 
}
```
Minimal, keeps token stream unchanged, adds non-required fields.

Maya (design): :thumbsup: I'll add a schema file and an SDK compatibility note.

Priya (eng-ml): I'll start the eval harness and coordinate with Liam for tenant prompts.

Liam (solutions): Reaching out to tenants now, will report back with samples and SLA feedback.

Ava (product): Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the intake record. I'll post the PRD link here when drafted. If you have quick wins (schema snippet, test skeleton), drop them in this thread.
